newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan wants North Korea to join informal talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan wants North Korea to join informal talks.

text.p: Senior Japanese officials urged North Korea on Wednesday to respond to their proposal for an unofficial meeting this weekend to discuss the return of Japanese wives of North Koreans.
"It's true that we haven't received any response from North Korea on the informal talks that we proposed for this weekend," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
Kajiyama said Pyongyang gave no reason for their lack of response, and added that Japan would continue to keep in contact with the communist government.
Tokyo and Pyongyang were scheduled to hold informal talks in early August following an earlier July meeting in Beijing of junior officials of the two countries.
The August meeting was to iron out details of a return by Japanese wives of North Koreans, among other issues.
Pyongyang announced last month that it may soon allow some of the estimated 1,800 Japanese wives who until then were not allowed to leave the communist country to visit their homeland.

"We cannot ignore the various issues which exist between the two governments and it is necessary to have proper inter-governmental talks," Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told reporters on Wednesday.
"We hope North Korea will take a positive attitude," Hashimoto said.

Kyodo news agency, quoting foreign ministry sources, said North Korea may want to start talks with Japan after the preparatory talks which started in New York on Tuesday for four-way negotiations between the United States, South Korea, North Korea and China for peace on the Korean peninsula.

Japan and North Korea have no diplomatic relations. The first round of Tokyo-Pyongyang normalisation talks began in 1989 but was suspended in 1992 after Japan accused North Korea of abducting a Japanese national.
